article_context: 围绕 Cal Newport 的“深度工作”、更灵活的任务规划以及有意识的停机时间展开，解释专注与放松如何共同提升效率，而不是把忙碌本身当作价值。

article.title: 阅读 Text 4 · 真正高效的人，不只会专注，也懂得“闲下来”
article.background: 围绕 Cal Newport 的“深度工作”、更灵活的任务规划以及有意识的停机时间展开，解释专注与放松如何共同提升效率，而不是把忙碌本身当作价值。

sentences.en: To combat the trap of putting a premium on being busy, Cal Newport, author of Deep Work: Rules for Focused Success in a Distracted World, recommends building a habit of "deep work" - the ability to focus without distraction.
sentences.zh: 为了摆脱“越忙越有价值”的陷阱，《深度工作：如何有效使用每一点脑力》的作者卡尔·纽波特建议培养“深度工作”的习惯，也就是不受干扰地专注。

segments.text: To combat the trap of putting a premium on being busy, Cal Newport, author of Deep Work: Rules for Focused Success in a Distracted World, recommends building a habit of "deep work" - the ability to focus without distraction.

sentences.en: There are a number of approaches to mastering the art of deep work - be it lengthy retreats dedicated to a specific task; developing a daily ritual; or taking a "journalistic" approach to seizing moments of deep work when you can throughout the day.
sentences.zh: 掌握深度工作的艺术有多种方法：可以长时间闭关，专心完成某项任务；可以建立每天固定的仪式；也可以采取“记者式”的做法，在一天中一有机会就抓住片刻投入深度工作。

segments.text: There are a number of approaches to mastering the art of deep work - be it lengthy retreats dedicated to a specific task; developing a daily ritual; or taking a "journalistic" approach to seizing moments of deep work when you can throughout the day.

sentences.en: Whichever approach, the key is to determine your length of focus time and stick to it.
sentences.zh: 无论采用哪种方法，关键都在于确定自己一次专注多长时间，并坚持执行。

segments.text: Whichever approach, the key is to determine your length of focus time and stick to it.

sentences.en: Newport also recommends "deep scheduling" to combat constant interruptions and get more done in less time.
sentences.zh: 纽波特还建议采用“深度排程”，以对抗不断出现的打扰，用更少的时间完成更多事情。

segments.text: Newport also recommends "deep scheduling" to combat constant interruptions and get more done in less time.

sentences.en: "At any given point, I should have deep work scheduled for roughly the next month.
sentences.zh: “在任何时候，我都应该把未来大约一个月的深度工作提前安排好。

segments.text: "At any given point, I should have deep work scheduled for roughly the next month.

sentences.en: Once on the calendar, I protect this time like I would a doctor's appointment or important meeting", he writes.
sentences.zh: 一旦写进日程表，我就会像保护一次就诊预约或重要会议那样保护这段时间。”他写道。

segments.text: Once on the calendar, I protect this time like I would a doctor's appointment or important meeting", he writes.

sentences.en: Another approach to getting more done in less time is to rethink how you prioritise your day - in particular how we craft our to-do lists.
sentences.zh: 另一种用更少时间做更多事情的方法，是重新思考一天中事情的优先次序，尤其是重新思考我们如何制定待办清单。

segments.text: Another approach to getting more done in less time is to rethink how you prioritise your day - in particular how we craft our to-do lists.

sentences.en: Tim Harford, author of Messy: The Power of Disorder to Transform Our Lives, points to a study in the early 1980s that divided undergraduates into two groups: some were advised to set out monthly goals and study activities; others were told to plan activities and goals in much more detail, day by day.
sentences.zh: 《混乱：无序如何改变我们的生活》的作者蒂姆·哈福德提到20世纪80年代初的一项研究：研究者把大学生分成两组，一组被建议列出每月目标和学习活动，另一组则被要求逐日制定详细得多的活动与目标。

segments.text: Tim Harford, author of Messy: The Power of Disorder to Transform Our Lives, points to a study in the early 1980s that divided undergraduates into two groups: some were advised to set out monthly goals and study activities; others were told to plan activities and goals in much more detail, day by day.

sentences.en: While the researchers assumed that the well-structured daily plans would be most effective when it came to the execution of tasks, they were wrong: the detailed daily plans demotivated students.
sentences.zh: 研究人员原以为，结构严密的每日计划在执行任务时最有效，但事实恰恰相反：过于详细的日计划削弱了学生的动力。

segments.text: While the researchers assumed that the well-structured daily plans would be most effective when it came to the execution of tasks, they were wrong: the detailed daily plans demotivated students.

sentences.en: Harford argues that inevitable distractions often render the daily to-do list ineffective, while leaving room for improvisation in such a list can reap the best results.
sentences.zh: 哈福德认为，无法避免的干扰常常会让每日待办清单失效；反倒是在清单中给临场调整留出空间，才可能取得最好的效果。

segments.text: Harford argues that inevitable distractions often render the daily to-do list ineffective, while leaving room for improvisation in such a list can reap the best results.

sentences.en: In order to make the most of our focus and energy, we also need to embrace downtime, or as Newport suggests, "be lazy".
sentences.zh: 要把我们的专注力和精力利用到极致，还需要接纳停下来休息的时间，或者用纽波特的话说，要“懒一点”。

segments.text: In order to make the most of our focus and energy, we also need to embrace downtime, or as Newport suggests, "be lazy".

sentences.en: "Idleness is not just a vacation, an indulgence or a vice; it is as indispensable to the brain as vitamin D is to the body ... [idleness] is, paradoxically, necessary to getting any work done," he argues.
sentences.zh: 他指出：“闲着并不只是一种休假、放纵或恶习；它之于大脑，就像维生素D之于身体一样不可或缺……矛盾的是，[闲下来]恰恰是完成任何工作的必要条件。”

segments.text: "Idleness is not just a vacation, an indulgence or a vice; it is as indispensable to the brain as vitamin D is to the body ... [idleness] is, paradoxically, necessary to getting any work done," he argues.

sentences.en: Srini Pillay, an assistant professor of psychiatry at Harvard Medical School, believes this counterintuitive link between downtime and productivity may be due to the way our brains operate.
sentences.zh: 哈佛医学院精神病学助理教授斯里尼·皮莱认为，休息与生产效率之间这种反直觉的联系，可能与大脑的运作方式有关。

segments.text: Srini Pillay, an assistant professor of psychiatry at Harvard Medical School, believes this counterintuitive link between downtime and productivity may be due to the way our brains operate.

sentences.en: When our brains switch between being focused and unfocused on a task, they tend to be more efficient.
sentences.zh: 当大脑在专注于任务与暂时不专注之间切换时，往往反而效率更高。

segments.text: When our brains switch between being focused and unfocused on a task, they tend to be more efficient.

sentences.en: "What people don't realise is that in order to complete these tasks they need to use both the focus and unfocus circuits in their brain," says Pillay.
sentences.zh: 皮莱说：“人们没有意识到的是，要完成这些任务，他们需要同时使用大脑中的专注回路和非专注回路。”

segments.text: "What people don't realise is that in order to complete these tasks they need to use both the focus and unfocus circuits in their brain," says Pillay.
